text:
alex: :rotating_light: Paging: Vela (customer, VPC + dedicated pool) is returning a large burst of 429s from their dedicated pool since ~2026-03-15T12:30Z. Customers report webhook failures and retry storms. Support ticket #12345 collecting details. @oncall-sre can you take?
ops-bot: ALERT: high-429-rate detected for tenant=vela pool=dedicated-velapool metric=rate_429 12:30-12:36 Z. Link: https://internal.redwood/telemetry/alerts/aler-vela-429 (auto-generated)
oncall-sre: Ack — grabbing the pager. Standing an incident call now. Will coordinate mitigation.
sana: How bad is customer impact? Any SLOs breached?
account-exec-jamie: Vela is enterprise, committed throughput 8k rps, soft limit 10k. They have critical customers on production. They're seeing failed webhooks. We need fast mitigation first, postmortem after.
grace: Short-term options: 1) emergency lift for tenant-specific quota 2) divert X% traffic to standby pool 3) ask customer to throttle concurrency. Which can we do quickly?
oncall-sre: We can request an emergency lift via rctl but it needs ops + product signoff. I'll request now if someone can confirm duration.
pm-luca: Product OK with temporary +2x quota for up to 2h while eng investigates. Approve. :thumbsup:
infra-engr-reed: I'm looking at infra traces — lots of 429s correlated with large payload requests and cold KV cache misses. Pool dedicated-velapool is seeing queue saturation on recv threads. Hypothesis: cache thrash + a sudden burst of long-context requests.
alex: Concrete plan: 1) Emergency lift for 2h 2) Divert 20% traffic to standby pool 3) Start an investigation task for eng-runtime (reed) 4) Tell Vela to reduce concurrency / disable retries for now 5) Create incident page and post to status.
alex: Command to request lift (internal):
```
rctl emergency-rate-lift --tenant vela --pool dedicated-velapool --duration 2h --reason "surge causing 429s" --by oncall-sre
```
deploy-bot: Runbook check: emergency-rate-lift requires approvals: ops (oncall-sre) + product (pm-luca). Audit will be stored at https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/emergency-rate-lift
ops-bot: action=alert_acknowledged user=oncall-sre request_id=req-9842
oncall-sre: Ops approved. pm-luca approved above. Executing lift now.
ops-bot: ACTION: emergency lift requested by oncall-sre. request_id=req-9842. Status: pending -> applied. New tenant limit applied: 20000 rps (was 10000).
sana: Quick logs snapshot (12:31-12:36Z):
```
[12:31:02Z] tenant=vela status=429 path=/api/generate rps=11234 tokens=... pool=dedicated-velapool
[12:31:05Z] tenant=vela status=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded backend_pool=dedicated-velapool concurrent=128
[12:33:10Z] tenant=vela status=200 path=/api/generate rps=13000 pool=standby-velapool
```
alex: After lift applied: diverting 20% traffic to standby-velapool via routing rule now. Command: `rctl route-set --tenant vela --percent 20 --target standby-velapool`
ops-bot: ROUTE UPDATE: tenant=vela route_change=20%->standby request_id=req-9843 status=applied
sana: Monitoring: 429 rate dropped from ~18% -> ~2% within 7 minutes of lift+divert, but p95 latency increased ~120ms. Still seeing some error bursts correlated with specific endpoints.
grace: Keep the lift in place while engineering digs. If root cause is cache thrash we should consider enforcing smaller payload limits or automatic model-fallback for this tenant.
infra-engr-reed: Collecting heap profiles and KV hit/miss rates. Quick grep shows many large messages from a single org within Vela tenant. I'll instrument prefix-caching metrics and check kernel-side queue lengths.
account-exec-jamie: I'll message Vela: "We've applied a temporary increase and are routing some traffic to standby. Could you pause aggressive retries for 30m and confirm if any particular client or endpoint is spiking?"
pm-luca: Also consider a short-term policy: if average token length > X then route to smaller model automatically. Not now for rollback risk, but note for follow-up.
oncall-sre: Owners and actions: eng-runtime = infra-engr-reed (investigation), infra = sana (monitoring + telemetry), account = account-exec-jamie (customer comms), product = pm-luca (approvals). I'll stay on watch for 30m then hand to weekday SRE.
infra-engr-reed: Found client_id=cli-982 with 10x usual avg payloads. Kicking off a query to list top offenders.
sana: I'll add an alert: if 429 > 1% for more than 10 mins after lift, auto-notify oncall-sre.
ops-bot: AUDIT: emergency-lift applied req-9842 by oncall-sre approved_by=pm-luca,ops. Link: https://internal.redwood/audit/req-9842
alex: Great work. Will create a short incident doc and schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow with eng-runtime and product. For now keep lift in place until we confirm steady state for 1 hour.
account-exec-jamie: Vela replied: "Thanks, we'll reduce concurrency and send logs for the flagged client_id." Good signal.
infra-engr-reed: Preliminary root cause: concentrated large-payload burst from a misconfigured integration + prefix-cache inefficiency. Fixes: 1) small-code patch to cache keying (low risk) 2) longer-term: tenant-level payload caps + automatic fallback. I'll open PR and target hotfix in next 2 hours.
grace: If PR looks small, we can canary deploy to standby pool first. Keep me looped.
oncall-sre: Handoff: I'll remain available until 13:30Z then pass to weekday SRE. Current status: emergency lift active, diversion 20% applied, 429s dropped to acceptable range, engineering investigating root cause. :white_check_mark:
alex: Summary + next steps: 1) keep temporary limit for 2h (req-9842) 2) monitor 429 and latency 3) reed to open PR + canary 4) jamie to keep customer informed 5) incident doc + postmortem tomorrow. Thanks team. :pray:
